profiles.description: Rounded upright rack and apparent tine placement broadly agree with preceding close view43; exact physical identity remains probable rather than certain.

profiles.name: Grain Bin Early Crown
profiles.description: Distinct branched antlers visible. Repeated rack form supports this encounter reference; cross-date identity remains provisional.

profiles.name: Hog Early Crown
profiles.description: Distinct branched antlers visible. Repeated rack form supports this encounter reference; cross-date identity remains provisional.

profiles.name: Hog Early Sweep
profiles.description: Low outward beam and sparse upright pattern repeats the separately visible far-left reference286.

profiles.name: Starkville Early Trident
profiles.description: Distinct branched antlers visible. Repeated rack form supports this encounter reference; cross-date identity remains provisional.

profiles.name: Grain Bin Mid Crown
profiles.description: Original W1050510 resolves developed branching rack; neighboring frame shows consistent side silhouette.

profiles.name: Cdub Mid Low Beam
profiles.description: Developed low forward beams and spaced uprights match close original W1069193 within local feeding sequence; no November identity asserted.

profiles.name: Hog Mid Round
profiles.description: Adjacent raised head agrees in round beam opening and upright arrangement with original SYFW00267; provisional within this local encounter.

profiles.name: Hog Mid Low Sweep
profiles.description: Raised left rack has the same low swept beam and spaced tine arrangement as original SYFW00837 in the same local sequence.

profiles.name: Coyote Arc
profiles.description: Wide spread, outer beam sweep and the paired inward uprights match W1047904 two minutes earlier.

profiles.name: Coyote Crest
profiles.description: The more closely packed row of long uprights matches the left-side rack in W1047901. The simultaneous Arc head at left prevents conflating the two animals.

profiles.name: Timber Eight
profiles.description: Typical eight-point outline with clear brow tines, tall middle uprights and curved outer beam ends. Full original comparison supports the same local identity within the 19:45–19:56 encounter.

profiles.name: Cdub Dusk Crown
profiles.description: Multi-tined rounded rack repeats on the right during the ongoing dusk encounter. Distinct from the small foreground fork buck visible simultaneously. Cross-date links to older profiles remain unresolved.

profiles.name: Cdub Daylight Tall
profiles.description: Long near-side beam carries several tall angular uprights and an extended forward end. Adjacent frames track the same buck entering left and feeding by the stand. Provisional encounter name may alias Cdub Daylight Tall or November Tall.

profiles.name: Rail Sweep
profiles.description: Long smooth outer beam ends curl upward. Fuller side view in 07835/07837 exposes clustered upright tines. Rack and body correspondence are visible through this 18-minute sequence.

profiles.name: Rail Longtine
profiles.description: Long, spaced uprights with a higher outer beam outline. Separate head is visible next to Rail Sweep throughout these checked frames.

profiles.name: Rail Cluster
profiles.description: Tighter, forward-projecting cluster of short upright tines is distinct from the two larger outlines in the same frame. New provisional local identity; score unmeasured.

profiles.name: Feeder Wide
profiles.description: Original reference or matching body, rack outline and temporal continuity within the W1028218–W1028226 encounter. Provisional local name only. Developed refers to visible branching and beam structure only; it does not establish a 120-inch score.

profiles.name: Feeder High
profiles.description: Original reference or matching body, rack outline and temporal continuity within the W1028218–W1028226 encounter. Provisional local name only. Developed refers to visible branching and beam structure only; it does not establish a 120-inch score.

profiles.name: Night Bow
profiles.description: Separate buck with heavy curved beams extending outward around the head. This is a local encounter reference and may duplicate an earlier named buck.

profiles.name: Cdub November Tall
profiles.description: Same upright-racked buck appears in consecutive daylight frames. Provisional encounter identity; resemblance to Cdub Daylight Tall remains an unresolved possible duplicate. Full rack is visible but score is unestablished.

profiles.name: Feeder Daylight
profiles.description: Clear daylight side/front-quarter view of a developed branched rack. Provisional encounter reference only. May be an alias of an existing Starkville buck; no earlier-name match or score is established.

accepted_aliases.evidence: Same right-facing side views in 07835/07837 and 08375 show a long nearly horizontal beam carrying the same ordered uprights, including the tallest middle tine, a shorter forward tine, and an upturned beam end. The clear reverse side in 08379 supports the rack comparison. These are local provisional identities, now one canonical identity.

The near-front 07833 and 08291 views share the asymmetric beam-end structure: close long prongs on the image-left side and a long inward-projecting diagonal tine below the tall outer beam on the image-right. Broad beam curvature, brow position and relative tine heights agree. The complementary 07825 and 08289 side-quarter views support this local match.

evidence: The Nov12 right-edge and Nov13 evening right-edge views are both left-facing at the same camera and similar distance.
Both show a broad outward main beam carrying a near-side sequence of tall uprights with a shorter forward point and an outer beam end that turns upward.
The brow/beam junction sits at similar height above the ear, and the far-side tines overlap in a similar clustered crown outline.
The Nov13 morning left-facing rack has the same broad multi-point outline, allowing for brighter illumination and a more frontal head rotation.
Both expose the right-facing side silhouette, which allows direct comparison without confusing opposite antlers.
A long, nearly level front portion of the main beam carries spaced uprights, with the posterior pair taller than the forward point.
The long brow tine rises close to the skull, with an angular open area between brow and the taller rear upright.
The overall beam projection relative to the muzzle/ear, the gap between dominant uprights and the curved forward beam termination agree.
evidence_frames: W1076545 close left head facing right

evidence: W1075439 exposes both rack halves from behind, with outward spreading main beams that turn up toward their tips, separated tall upright tines and lower brow branches near the skull.
W1075445 turns that rack to the same left-facing profile as Dusk W1075126. The relative positions of the tall rear uprights, shorter forward point and outer terminal beam agree.
The same silhouette appears on Nov13 Wide right-edge W1076255, strengthening the link across viewing angles.
The front-quarter W1075573 view shows a rounded, broad opening with main beams rising around the outside and a tall set of upright points above each brow area.
W1075439 provides the reverse view: its paired beam curves and the relative tall upright placement agree with the forward view, allowing for a different head tilt.
The branching arrangement is compatible with the Dusk/Wide side silhouettes, and no opposing persistent tine break or reversed asymmetry is visible.
This match uses the combination of front, reverse and side rack outlines; resemblance to a similar profile name is not evidence.
